newsitem.title: CHINA: China says little chance of more big tremors soon.
newsitem.headline: China says little chance of more big tremors soon.

text.p: An offshore earthquake measuring 6.1 on the Richter scale shook the Yellow Sea near eastern China's Shanghai late on Saturday, but no casualties were reported, a State Seismological Bureau official said.
"Currently, there's no (report of) damage or injuries whatsoever," the official said by telephone. "There shouldn't be any, because it was 100-200 km (60-125 miles) from the coast."
The quake, which hit at 9.56 p.m. (1356 GMT), measured 6.1 on the Richter scale and had its epicentre more than 100 km off the China coast in the Yellow Sea.

A senior official from China's State Earthquake Bureau was quoted by Xinhua news agency as saying on Sunday that there was little chance of further big tremors in the immediate future in the East China area.
The bureau official said 25 aftershocks from the earthquake had been recorded, the biggest registering 3.0 on the Richter scale.

"The chance of an earthquake bigger than this in the southern Yellow Sea quake zone any time soon is relatively small and another quake of a similar scale would anyway have little impact on the Shanghai area," the official said.
The news agency reported said that "it is understood that the masses in Shanghai, Zhejiang province and Jiangsu province are relatively calm."
Scientists say China is currently passing through a period of particularly high seismological activity.
In September, a minor tremor injured 17 people in southwestern Yunnan province's Lijiang county, where at least 304 people were killed in February by an earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale.
The February quake damaged more than 1.17 million homes, completely destroyed 340,000, left 160,000 people without shelter and caused huge economic damage, local officials said.
